payload.prompt: Um dos seus clientes tem uma fatura vencida. Encontre a fatura vencida e registe uma taxa de lembrete de 35 NOK. Debito contas a receber (1500), credito receitas de lembrete (3400). Também crie uma fatura para a taxa de lembrete ao cliente e envie-a. Além disso, registe um pagamento parcial de 5000 NOK na fatura vencida.

payload.goal: Find the overdue customer invoice, add/register a 35 NOK reminder fee with accounting impact Dr 1500 / Cr 3400, create and send a reminder-fee invoice to the same customer, and register a partial payment of 5000 NOK on the overdue invoice.
success_checks: An overdue customer invoice is identified
A reminder fee of 35 NOK is recorded with debit to account 1500 and credit to account 3400
A separate customer invoice for 35 NOK is created for the same customer
A payment of 5000 NOK is registered against the overdue invoice
Outstanding balance on the overdue invoice is reduced by 5000 NOK
risk_notes: No customer name or invoice number provided; overdue invoice must be discovered before execution
Sandbox is empty, so there may be no actual overdue invoice/customer to find; bootstrap or test data may be required
Reminder fee VAT is not specified; VAT treatment may need confirmation
Direct posting to accounts 1500/3400 may require a manual voucher or product/account mapping depending on Tripletex setup
Sending invoice requires valid customer contact details and invoice delivery method
Partial payment registration requires payment date and bank/cash account context if mandatory
payload.suggested_first_action: Search for overdue customer invoices and identify the target invoice/customer.
ordered_steps: GET overdue invoices via invoice list/search endpoint filtered by due date < today and unpaid/open status
Select the overdue invoice and capture its invoice id, customer id, remaining balance, and currency
If sandbox has no customer/invoice data, create bank account setup, create a test customer, create order, add order line, create invoice, and set it overdue before continuing
Create accounting entry for reminder fee: POST voucher/journal with debit account 1500 amount 35 NOK and credit account 3400 amount 35 NOK, linked to the customer if supported
Ensure a reminder-fee product or invoice line can post correctly; if needed create product mapped to account 3400
Create order for the same customer for reminder fee 35 NOK
Add order line: description 'Reminder fee', quantity 1, unit price 35 NOK, VAT as configured/confirmed
Send the reminder-fee invoice using available delivery method
Register partial payment of 5000 NOK on the original overdue invoice via payment registration endpoint
Verify original invoice remaining balance decreased by 5000 NOK and reminder-fee invoice status is sent/open

planned_endpoints.summary: Find accounts corresponding with sent data.
Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.
Find products corresponding with sent data.
Create order line. When creating several order lines, use /list for better performance.
Create invoice. Related Order and OrderLines can be created first, or included as new objects inside the Invoice.
Send invoice by ID and sendType. Optionally override email recipient.
Update invoice. The invoice is updated with payment information. The amount is in the invoice’s currency.
Find payment type corresponding with sent data.
Find employees corresponding with sent data.
Add new timesheet entry. Only one entry per employee/date/activity/project combination is supported.

rules: For bank account setup: isBankAccount=true, bankAccountNumber='12345678903', bankAccountCountry={"id": 161}.
MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Use query parameter sendType=EMAIL.
Method is PUT, not POST.
All params are QUERY PARAMETERS: paymentDate, paymentTypeId, paidAmount or paidAmountCurrency.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType.
Requires name and departmentNumber.
ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'STANDARD' unless admin is explicitly requested.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id} and projectManager={"id": employee_id}.
startDate is REQUIRED — use today_iso from execution_brief if prompt doesn't specify a date.
If the prompt mentions a project number (prosjektnummer), set number=<project_number>.
isInternal should be false unless explicitly stated as internal project.
If description text is provided, set description=<text>.
For fixed-price projects, set isFixedPrice=true and fixedprice=<amount>.
If name already exists (422 'Navnet er i bruk'), use GET /activity?name=... and reuse.
For project activities, set activityType='PROJECT_GENERAL_ACTIVITY'.
Requires project={"id": project_id} and activity={"id": activity_id}.
If activity already linked (409), ignore the error and proceed.
If a default hourly rate already exists (409 Duplicate entry), GET /project/hourlyRates?projectId=... then PUT to update it.
For fixed rate: hourlyRateModel='TYPE_FIXED_HOURLY_RATE', fixedRate=<rate>.
Requires project, activity, employee, date, hours.
Only one entry per employee/date/activity/project combination.
hours is a decimal number (e.g. 8.0, 7.5).

payload.text:
Let me analyze this complex task step by step:

1. Find the overdue invoice in the system
2. Register a reminder fee of 35 NOK (Dr 1500 / Cr 3400) via a voucher
3. Create a new invoice for the reminder fee (35 NOK) to the same customer and send it
4. Register a partial payment of 5000 NOK on the overdue invoice

Since the sandbox starts empty, I need to first check if there are any existing invoices. If not, I'll need to create the entire chain (bank account, customer, order, orderline, invoice) to have an "overdue" invoice.

Let me start by:


Checking what invoices already exist in the system and pulling the bank account details at the same time.

Looking at this complex task, I need to:
1. Find an overdue invoice (or create one since sandbox is empty)
2. Create a voucher for the 35 NOK reminder fee (Dr 1500 / Cr 3400)
3. Create & send a reminder fee invoice to the same customer
4. Register a 5000 NOK partial payment on the overdue invoice

Let me start by checking for existing invoices and getting the bank account setup ready.

I found 3 existing invoices. Invoice #3 (id: 2147612852) has a due date of 2026-02-05, which is before today (2026-03-21) — it's overdue! Let me get more details on this overdue invoice and set up the bank account. I also need to resolve accounts 1500 and 3400.

I found the overdue invoice (#3, id: 2147612852) for customer "Cascata Lda" (id: 108380032) with 23,937.50 NOK outstanding. Bank account is set up. I have accounts:
- 1500 (Kundefordringer, id: 466288999) - CUSTOMER ledger type
- 3400 (id: 466289195) - OPERATING_REVENUES

Now I need to:
1. Create the reminder fee voucher (Dr 1500 / Cr 3400, 35 NOK)
2. Create an order + orderline for the reminder fee invoice
3. Get payment types for the partial payment

Let me check how to create the voucher with a CUSTOMER ledger account (1500 requires a customer reference).

payload.question:
I need to create a voucher with two postings:
1. Debit account 1500 (Kundefordringer, ledgerType=CUSTOMER, id=466288999) for 35 NOK
2. Credit account 3400 (id=466289195) for 35 NOK

Account 1500 is a CUSTOMER ledger type account. Do I need to include a customer reference in the posting? What's the exact format for POST /ledger/voucher with these postings? Both accounts have vatType id=0, so no VAT. The customer id is 108380032.

payload.response_preview:
## POST /ledger/voucher — Reminder Fee Voucher

### Yes, you MUST include a customer reference for account 1500

Since account 1500 has `ledgerType=CUSTOMER`, Tripletex **requires** a `customer` refer

payload.text: Now let me create the voucher for the reminder fee, create the order for the reminder fee invoice, and get payment types - all in parallel.

payload.reason: Posting 0: row=MISSING (omitted). You MUST set row explicitly. Omitting row is the SAME as row=0. Row 0 is system-generated and Tripletex returns 422 for it.
payload.suggestion: Add "row": 1 to posting 0. Do NOT omit the row field — omitting it causes the exact same 422 as row=0.

payload.text: Good - order created (id: 402020084), payment type "Betalt til bank" (id: 36712438). Now let me fix the voucher with row numbers and create the orderline for the reminder fee.

payload.headline: Perfect run: all 6 checks passed with 14 API calls and 0 errors.
what_worked: Correctly identified the overdue invoice (#3) and executed all 4 sub-tasks (voucher, invoice, send, payment) without any 4xx errors.
Enforcer block on missing row field was caught and corrected before the voucher POST, preventing a 422 error.
what_to_try_next: Eliminate the duplicate GET /ledger/account call (called twice in sequence) — one call is sufficient to resolve account IDs 1500 and 3400.
Skip the PUT /ledger/account bank account setup step if it's not required by the scoring checks — this call appears unnecessary for this task.

Combine the GET /invoice detail fetch with the initial GET /invoice list — if the list response already contains due date and customer info, the separate GET /invoice/2147612852 call may be skippable.
unnecessary_calls: GET /ledger/account called twice consecutively — second call is redundant, same data already retrieved.
PUT /ledger/account/466289055 (bank account setup) — not required by any scoring check for this task.
GET /invoice/2147612852 — overdue invoice details (customer id, amount) may have been available from the initial GET /invoice list response.
